analyzed_vuln.description: `htmlParseChunk` saves offsets into the parser input buffer, calls `xmlParserInputBufferPush`, but on `res < 0` returns at lines 6139-6142 before `xmlBufSetInputBaseCur` rebases `ctxt->input->{base,cur,end}`. With an active character encoder, the push can grow/reallocate the converted `xmlBuf` and then fail conversion, leaving those parser pointers aimed into the freed pre-realloc allocation. The later terminating parse reports an encoder error, and `xmlParserPrintFileContextInternal` dereferences the dangling `input->cur` (crash in `error.c:194`). The final call's attempted rebase is also ineffective because `xmlBufSetInputBaseCur` rejects a buffer already marked errored and its return is ignored.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: The HTML push parser must first process a `<meta charset=...>` that installs an encoder (the PoV selects EUC-JP), then receive chunked data containing malformed/incomplete bytes such that `xmlParserInputBufferPush` invokes `xmlCharEncInput`; conversion grows/reallocates the converted buffer and subsequently returns an encoding error. The fuzz harness feeds the document in 128-byte chunks and ignores the failed nonterminating `htmlParseChunk` return, then calls `htmlParseChunk(ctxt, NULL, 0, 1)`. That final call raises an error while the input pointers remain stale, causing the heap-use-after-free during error-context printing.

args: Analyze the stale parser input pointer vulnerability in htmlParseChunk in libxml2/HTMLparser.c around lines 6139-6155. In particular, after saving base/cur offsets and calling xmlParserInputBufferPush, how should ctxt->input base/cur/end safely be rebased if the converted xmlBuf reallocates and then becomes errored? Compare patterns elsewhere in the project and explain whether xmlBufSetInputBaseCur can operate on errored buffers or whether direct pointer reconstruction / another API is appropriate.

The ASan report shows a UAF in error.c:194 after htmlParseChunk returns immediately when xmlParserInputBufferPush reports an encoding failure. An active EUC-JP encoder caused xmlCharEncInput to grow/realloc the converted buffer before conversion failed, so ctxt->input pointers still point into freed storage. The terminating harness call later raises an encoder error and context printing reads input->cur. Vulnerability details additionally say a later xmlBufSetInputBaseCur attempt is ineffective because that API rejects an errored xmlBuf and its return is ignored. I am inspecting HTMLparser.c, buf.c, and xmlIO.c and want the narrow root-cause fix, including established parser patterns for rebasing after failed pushes.
